clue.text: Diaghilev's clue for "stream"?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: the ballet impresario Diaghilev setting a crossword clue
setter's reading: a phrase that would clue the word stream, with an order word followed by a rearrangeable word

explanation.surface: The great Russian impresario of the Ballets Russes tries his hand at setting a crossword clue.
explanation.walkthrough: DANCING MASTER is a clue for STREAM: 'dancing' tells you to rearrange MASTER, which makes STREAM. Diaghilev, who ran a ballet company, was himself a dancing master.
explanation.definitionFit: Diaghilev directed and trained ballet dancers, so he was a teacher of dance, and the phrase also works as wordplay for the word stream.

clue.text: A right way for Romans to date the song of the tree

parts.note: taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for right
ab urbe condita, 'from the founding of the city', the Roman way of numbering years
an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: A Latin lesson on Roman calendars drifts into a song about a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the setter's own pseudonym, Araucaria, which is the monkey-puzzle tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Araucaria is the botanical genus of the monkey-puzzle and related conifers.

clue.text: Ring in the man who said Eureka!

indicators.note: the answer lies within the name of the person described, so only letters inside it are kept and the ends are dropped

parts.note: Archimedes cried Eureka on discovering displacement in his bath

explanation.surface: A bell sounds inside the man who shouted Eureka.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually the answer is inside a name the solver must first work out from a description: Archimedes, whose outer letters are shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A chime is the ringing sound of bells, and to chime is to ring.

clue.text: High time to go forward in agreement, I agree

indicators.note: the going-forward word is placed inside the word for agreement

parts.note: a nod signals agreement
on, as in 'go on', means forward
ay (aye) is a yes

explanation.surface: Someone nods along to a decision that it is high time to press on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High time' looks like the idiom for overdue; here it means the time when the sun is highest.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is when the sun stands highest, so noonday is literally the high point of the day, as in 'high noon'.

clue.text: Horse 'as to be strung up?

parts.note: 'as to is 'has to', with the H dropped Cockney-fashion
to be strung up is to hang

explanation.surface: A Cockney declares that some horse deserves to be hanged.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'as tells you to drop the H of HANG too, giving the Cockney MUST 'ANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a small wild horse of the American plains.

clue.text: Don't make any loans in the branch? There's glory for you!

indicators.note: the refusal to lend is placed inside the word for a branch

parts.note: a spur is a branch line or offshoot
read as 'lend nought', making a loan of zero

explanation.surface: A bank branch decides to stop lending, and someone sarcastically calls that glorious.
explanation.walkthrough: The loans word is read as LEND O, lending nothing, with O for zero; it sits inside SP-UR.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour means magnificent brilliance or grandeur, a close synonym of glory.

clue.text: King lives in an 18

indicators.note: 18 across is the word for a jumble of letters, so 'in an 18' says these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that a king lives on in some mysterious way.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 18 across, ANAGRAM. 'The King lives' is also the familiar rumour about Elvis Presley.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley was famously nicknamed the King of Rock and Roll.

clue.text: Explore just one avenue — also begin instilling fear of surviving angels?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: investigating only a single possibility

definitions.text: begin instilling fear of surviving angels?
definitions.meaning: setter's reading: overturn a single rock and startle a winged creature into flight

explanation.surface: Advice on research narrowing to one line of enquiry, with a strange turn about frightening angels.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a line from Francis Thompson's poem 'The Kingdom of God': 'The angels keep their ancient places; Turn but a stone and start a wing!'
explanation.definitionFit: Overturning only one stone is exploring a single avenue, and to start a wing is to startle an angel, which still keeps its ancient place.

clue.text: See 8
Do you hear, you goat? Rodent's nearly of the same mind

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the rodent goes
asks the solver to listen, so the next words count by their sound

parts.note: a nanny is a female goat
a mouse is a rodent

explanation.surface: Someone insults a person as a goat while muttering about a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: Unanimous describes a group in which everyone agrees, all sharing one view.

clue.text: Animate number in property right

indicators.note: the number is placed inside the legal term

parts.note: a lien is a right to keep someone's property until a debt is paid
the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A legal note about a number written into a property right, with 'Animate' sounding like a cartoon instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To liven or animate something is to bring life and energy to it.

clue.text: Hospital situated in pleasant little corner

indicators.note: something situated in another thing sits inside it

parts.note: a direct synonym
H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital tucked away in a pleasant little corner of town.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a small recess or nook, a little corner set into something.

clue.text: Analysis of what's wrong in digs, as nothing else can be seen

indicators.note: else means otherwise, so these letters are to be set out otherwise

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
O looks like a zero

explanation.surface: Someone works out what is wrong in their lodgings when nothing else is visible.
explanation.walkthrough: Digs is British slang for rented lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagnosis is the identification of what is wrong, especially of an illness from its symptoms.

clue.text: No scout and (for Anglo-Saxon king) no scholar

definitions.meaning: first meaning: not prepared, unlike a Scout, whose motto is 'Be Prepared'
second meaning, split un-read-y: not well read

explanation.walkthrough: Ethelred the Unready was an Anglo-Saxon king of England; his nickname originally meant 'ill-advised' but is now taken as 'unprepared'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unprepared contradicts the Scout motto, while reading it as unread suggests a person lacking scholarship.

clue.text: Not having to be argued about, which is pleasant

definitions.text: Not having to be argued about
definitions.meaning: first meaning: capable of being agreed without dispute
second meaning: nice to be with

explanation.surface: Someone praises a point that is beyond dispute as a pleasant thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as agree-able it means something people can accept without dispute, while the everyday sense is pleasing or likeable.

clue.text: Country or state on my mind?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the nation in the Caucasus

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the place they keep thinking of is a nation or a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgia names both a Caucasian republic and a southern American state, the subject of the Hoagy Carmichael standard.

clue.text: I have no experience of the colour of the sea at the cape

definitions.note: first-person description of the person the noun names

parts.note: the sea is often described as green
Cape Horn, the southern tip of South America

explanation.surface: A novice sailor admits never having rounded the cape or seen its sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is a newcomer or novice lacking experience, so the word says of itself that it has none.

clue.text: A pair of beasts to make a muddle

parts.note: taken as written
a nag (an old horse) and a ram (a male sheep)

explanation.surface: Two animals get loose and make a mess of things.
explanation.definitionFit: An anagram jumbles the letters of a word or phrase into a different order.

clue.text: Accompaniments of door in spa

parts.note: a doormat lies by a door
a lock is fitted to a door

explanation.surface: Fittings for a door in a spa hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Two things that go with a door, a mat and a lock; MATLOCK (Bath) is a spa town in Derbyshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Matlock and Matlock Bath in the Peak District grew as Victorian spa towns around their thermal springs.

clue.text: Hot iron in French opening

parts.note: fer is French for iron
a vent is an opening for air

explanation.surface: A hot iron poked into a French opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal but only belongs with 'French'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervent means passionate, burning with feeling; it comes from the Latin for boiling.

clue.text: More than cross to hide notes?

parts.note: an animal's hide or pelt
IOUs are notes promising repayment

explanation.surface: Someone is furious at being made to hide promissory notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious means intensely angry, a degree beyond merely cross.

clue.text: One harassing people in the hills

indicators.note: the people sit between two hills

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, and two of them make hills
people as men

explanation.surface: A bandit preys on travellers up in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: Tor is a word for a craggy hill, common on Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is someone who harasses or persecutes others, causing distress.

clue.text: Pictorial pun about transport

parts.note: re means concerning
a bus is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A cartoon joke about public transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle that represents words through pictures and symbols, punning on their sounds.

clue.text: Piece of bodily tissue: corollary being "Imp.old"?

parts.note: the counterpart of imperial measures is the SI or metric system
the counterpart of old is new

explanation.surface: A medical note about tissue with a cryptic aside about an old imp.
explanation.walkthrough: If imperial measures are old, it follows that SI units (the metric Système International) are new: the corollary flips both words.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinew is a tendon, the tough fibrous tissue joining muscle to bone.

clue.text: Here volumes are drunk in propria persona?

indicators.note: a drunk person is all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Latin for 'in one's own person', that is, in the flesh

explanation.surface: Someone appears in person at a library while drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Books, or volumes, stand on a shelf, so a shelf is where volumes are kept.

clue.text: Plutocrat puts sodium on old coin

parts.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium
a bob was a shilling in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: A rich man lays salt on an antique coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob was a European who made a fortune in India, hence any very wealthy, powerful person.

clue.text: Two ciphers put into the ground alone

parts.note: two zeros: O and none
seeds sown are put into the ground

explanation.surface: Two zeros get buried in the ground, with nobody else around.
explanation.walkthrough: A cipher is a zero, a nonentity: one is O, the other NONE.
explanation.definitionFit: On one's own means by oneself, without company or help.

clue.text: … whatever anybody else may say, I say Eureka!

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a stubborn speaker sticks to their own view
setter's reading: Eureka is Greek for 'I have found', so this speaker voices a discovery

explanation.surface: A blunt person insists on their own verdict, then cries out as if they had found something.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening dots continue from 3 down's Archimedes. To say 'Eureka' is literally to speak 'I find'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means plain speaking regardless of others, and it puns on Eureka, which means a declaration of having found something.
